The seven-time champion was left 'extremely frustrated' after qualifying in Hungary, with the Ferrari pit wall taking the brunt of his ire. In the first instance, Hamilton claimed to be 'shocked' that the team elected to run first for the final laps in qualifying, denying the chance to set a time when the track was at its theoretical best. But having completed his lap, Hamilton was then not informed of a charging Oscar Piastri behind, who had just begun his effort, something that ultimately resulted in the Briton being handed a three-place grid penalty for impeding the McLaren driver at Turn 1. Hamilton was pipped to pole by Norris Read Also F1 champion hails Hamilton for using 'power' in sport to progress at Ferrari Lewis Hamilton branded UFC champion a “coward” after airborne pig hunt "Sometimes you just can’t catch a break," wrote Hamilton on social media. "Another weekend when I’ve been feeling great throughout all the sessions, but then it just falls apart. To go from being so close to pole to then starting P5 is extremely frustrating. "I always do my best to keep positive — sport is always about the highs and lows, but it’s also in the margins. Every point counts and you have to seize every opportunity." Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT The penalty is Hamilton's third in as many weekends, after being handed five-second sanctions at both Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps for a false start and causing a collision, respectively. Show Instagram Embedded Content Loading this video will expose you to potential cookies and tracking by the provider "After 3 penalties in 3 weekends, it’s becoming difficult to hang on to that positivity. Still, I won’t let the setbacks take away from the progress we’ve been making as a team. With the pace we have, I’m hopeful we can get something out of the race tomorrow. The car has been feeling better and better, and we’ve been competitive all weekend. "Tonight, we’ll keep working hard together to give ourselves the best possible chance tomorrow. I always enjoy this track, so keep the faith and send good vibes for the race." A silver lining for the Ferrari driver will be that his latest penalty moves him onto the more favourable clean side of the grid, something that is historically an advantage at the Hungaroring. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP View image in fullscreen Prime minister Anthony Albanese said he was optimistic Pacific countries would support Australia’s bid to join the UN security council. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP Anthony Albanese Albanese launches bid for UN security council seat and names former Murdoch aide to top diplomatic post Australia and Finland are vying for a spot on the council, and the PM needs two thirds of member states to back him Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Sun 20 Sep 2026 17.45 EDT Last modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 20.37 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Australia having a seat at the United Nations Security Council will be able to help with the cost of living back home, the prime minister insists. Anthony Albanese has launched a formal bid for Australia to serve a two-year term on the UN security council in 2029 and 2030. Albanese also defended former News Corp head of broadcasting Siobhan McKenna as Australia’s next consul general to New York. A vote for the UN council spot won’t be held until mid 2028, but lobbying efforts will intensify during the prime minister’s visit to New York for the UN general assembly. The prime minister said Australia’s role on the council would be able to benefit ordinary citizens. “Engagement with the world matters. It matters because it makes a difference to the cost of living, to inflation, to Australians’ way of life,” he told reporters in New York on Monday, Australian time. “That is why we can’t afford to not be engaged with the world, because it has a direct impact on the quality of life of Australians on a day-to-day basis. As China rises, Australia is increasingly enmeshed in the US war machine. Is the alliance still worth the risk? Read more “We have an opportunity through this potential seat on the UN security council to play a key role in shaping the global issues that really matter to Australians.” Australia has served on the security council five times since the UN was established after the second world war. The most recent stint was in 2013 and 2014, where Australia was able to lead a response to the Russian downing of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17. View image in fullscreen Anthony Albanese unveiled former News Corp head of broadcasting Siobhan McKenna as Australia’s next consul general to New York. Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty Images Albanese said the role Australia played during that period was evidence of what a spot on the council could achieve. “We do need to stand up to the Middle East conflict. I think there is a role for middle powers to engage, and Australia has done that as we’ve engaged with the war in Ukraine in the coalition of the willing,” he said. Two countries are elected to the security council from the Western Europe and Others group, which includes Australia. So far, only Australia and Finland have put their hands up for a spot on the council, but other countries from the bloc could still launch bids. Even if the two countries run unopposed, Australia would still need support from two-thirds of the 193 UN member states to be successful. Of the 15 members on the security council, China, France, the US, UK and Russia are permanent members, while the remainder serve two-year terms. The prime minister said he was optimistic of getting support from Pacific nations, as well as south-east Asian countries in the Asean pact. Part of the campaign will seek to leverage Australia’s role in the Pacific and action on climate change in the region. The campaign, called “we listen, we partner, we protect”, will also focus on aiming to boost the voices of middle powers and smaller nations in the UN. Action taken by Australia to be the first country in the world to ban people under 16 from using social media will be at the forefront of the campaign, as well as recent efforts to place guardrails on the expanding use of AI. During the press conference, Albanese was asked whether he had sought assurances McKenna wouldn’t “continue to lobby or deal with Mr Murdoch in advancing business interests” but the prime minister did not confirm. “Siobhan McKenna is a professional, and she will do an outstanding job representing Australia and the Australian government here in New York,” he said in response. “And the fact that she has experience in both the private sector and the public sector is a very good thing. I’m someone who supports people being appointed on merit. Siobhan McKenna has been appointed on merit.” McKenna, the chair of Australia Post and former chair of the NBN, will take up the role later in the year. Multiple media outlets, including The Financial Times , recently reported on American intelligence sharing information on Huang's extramarital affair with a Chinese woman. The woman, according to US intelligence sources, had been recruited by China 's Ministry of State Security. Chipmaker NVIDIA profits up, despite trade war challenges To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The reports identified her as an executive for Singapore-based company Megaspeed. The US is investigating the company over suspicions that it was helping Beijing bypass export restrictions and obtain cutting-edge AI chips . According to The New York Times , the company has bought Nvidia chips worth billions of dollars in the last two years. US lawmakers have invited the Nvidia chief to brief them on the reports. Nvidia's Huang as rich as Warren Buffet On Sunday, Nvidia's top executive admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife of 40 years. "My actions hurt her and our children," Jensen Huang wrote in an email sent to Nvidia staff. "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." Nvidia's AI PC explained: AI agents, speed and data privacy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video He also said he was he committed to protecting the company and "supporting America's national security." Huang was born in Taipei and spent part of his childhood in Taiwan before moving to the US. In 1993, he and two other people launched Nvidia, a company that grew to become a leading manufacturer of computer graphic cards and then an essential supplier of computer chips in the AI boom . Nvidia's Cage for AI: can it prevent disaster? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The 63-year-old Nvidia CEO is one of the richest people in the world, according to the Forbes magazine, with his $162.2 billion (€145.5 billion) net worth as of Sunday putting him roughly on par with globally renowned investor Warren Buffet. Huang stays on as Nvidia CEO In their statement, Nvidia's board of directors said Huang will remain the head of the US-based company while the probe is taking place. Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," according to their statement. The board said a group of "independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation." At the same time, the heads of the $4.5 trillion company said they had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/.text: Extremiștii de la AfD ajung în această săptămână în Capitală. Formațiunea germană a fost invitată de AUR la o serie de evenimente care vor avea loc la Palatul Parlamentului. Vizita vine la scurt timp după ce lidera partidului german i-a atacat pe românii din Germania , pe care i-a acuzat că abuzează de sistemul de asistență socială. „Veți avea oportunitatea de a le pune întrebări, să vedem dacă au vrut cu adevărat să spună ceea ce noi am interpretat că este o ofensă la adresa tuturor românilor care muncesc corect, legal în Germania. Foarte mulți români care sunt stabiliți acolo cu acte, legal, cu cetățenie sunt susținători și votanți AfD. Nu putem să stricăm relațiile cu un partid pentru o declarație care trebuie lămurită, pentru că sunt unele voci care spun că doamna Weidel nu a vrut să spună acest lucru. Iată, vom avea o oportunitate să ne clarificăm cu toții”, a declarat într-o conferință de presă Cristina Dumitrescu, purtătorul de cuvânt al AUR. Alice Weidel, șefa extremei drepte din Germania, i-a acuzat pe imigranții din România că „jefuiesc sistemul social”. Aceasta a distribuit pe X un documentar despre imigranții români și a dat exemplul orașului Magdeburg, unde cheltuielile cu cetățenii români au crescut de 20 de ori și au ajuns la trei milioane de euro pe an. Comunitatea românească din Germania este formată din aproximativ 900 de mii de oameni. Fragment din documentarul difuzat: „Gunoi, zgomot și agitație în cartierul acela. De ani de zile, noii veniți din România și Bulgaria sunt învinuiți pentru aceste condiții. Din 2014, cetățenii UE din aceste țări au libertatea de a se stabili oriunde. Chiar și apartamentele de acest gen sunt plătite de centrele de ocupare a forței de muncă din Germania” . AUR susține că reprezentanții AfD nu vor participa la protestul care va avea loc în aceeași perioadă în parcul Izvor, în fața Palatului Parlamentului, manifestație la care partidul condus de George Simion își va trimite susținătorii. „Sunt două lucruri diferite. Cei de la AfD au fost invitați în urmă cu mai mult timp la conferințele internaționale pe care noi le vom desfășura pe întreg parcursul acestui weekend. Nu este vorba de participarea lor la protest, ci este vorba de participarea lor la niște conferințe”, a precizat Cristina Dumitrescu. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News
